subject: english-studies
title: Action words (verbs)
summary: Find the words that tell us what someone or something does.

lesson.text: Some words tell us what someone or something does. They are called action words, or verbs.
In each sentence, the action word is: runs, cries, cooks, sing.
Ask: what is the person or thing doing? The word that answers is the action word.

lesson.title: The boy kicks the ball.
steps: Who is in the sentence? The boy.
What is the boy doing? He kicks.
"Boy" and "ball" are naming words, not action words.

lesson.text: You can act out most action words: jump, clap, sit, eat, write, dance, sweep. If you can do it, it is probably an action word.
Play "Simon says" at home. Every instruction ("Simon says jump") uses an action word.

questions.prompt: Which word is an action word?
questions.explanation: You can jump, so jump is an action word. Table and Lagos are naming words; red describes a colour.

questions.prompt: Find the action word: Mama sells tomatoes.
questions.explanation: What does Mama do? She sells. Mama and tomatoes are naming words.

questions.prompt: Find the action word: The dog barks at night.
questions.explanation: What does the dog do? It barks. Dog and night are naming words.

questions.prompt: Choose the best action word: The girls ___ to the music.
questions.explanation: The gap needs something the girls do. "The girls dance to the music." Chair and school are things, and happy is not an action.
